question_text: Chemical analysis in materials science laboratories is frequently done by means of the scanning electron microscope. In this instrument, an electron beam generates characteristic x-rays that can be used to identify chemical elements. This instrument samples a roughly cylindrical volume at the surface of a solid material. Calculate the number of atoms sampled in a $1-\mu \mathrm{m}$-diameter by $1-\mu \mathrm{m}$-deep cylinder in the surface of solid copper. Assuming $\text { density of copper }=8.93 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{cm}^{3}$ and $\text { atomic mass of copper }=63.55 \mathrm{amu}$.The unit of the answer is atoms.
response:
## Reasoning

The SEM samples a cylindrical volume: diameter = 1 μm, depth = 1 μm, so radius $r = 0.5\;\mu\text{m}$.

**1. Volume of the cylinder**

$$V = \pi r^{2} h = \pi(0.5\;\mu\text{m})^{2}(1\;\mu\text{m}) = 0.25\pi\;\mu\text{m}^{3}$$

Converting to cm³ ($1\;\mu\text{m} = 10^{-4}\,\text{cm}$, so $1\;\mu\text{m}^{3}=10^{-12}\,\text{cm}^{3}$):

$$V = 0.25\pi \times 10^{-12}\;\text{cm}^{3} \approx 7.854\times10^{-13}\;\text{cm}^{3}$$

**2. Mass of copper in that volume**

$$m = \rho V = 8.93 \times 7.854\times10^{-13} \approx 7.01\times10^{-12}\;\text{g}$$

**3. Number of atoms**

$$N = \frac{m\,N_{A}}{M} = \frac{(7.01\times10^{-12})(6.022\times10^{23})}{63.55} \approx 6.65\times10^{10}$$

$$\boxed{6.65\times10^{10}}$$
